main_body: A flat dark-green grass ground patch (4x3 tiles) with a repeating tile of scattered lighter blades, dark clumps, and a few yellow and red flower pixels
top_band: none - flat ground texture, no standing volume; the surface is a uniform top-down terrain fill
evidence: This is a terrain ground tile, not a standing object, so the top/front contract does not apply. It is a seamless grass fill with no vertical face, no isometric side face and no elevation drawing. As terrain it is acceptable under the kind definition.

style.evidence: The candidate has a dark olive base with 3-4 greens (base, mid blade, light blade, dark clump) plus sparse yellow and red accent pixels, so it is not a flat fill. Texture is a very regular tile repeat: the same blade clumps recur every 16px, which makes the patterning obvious. Compared with the Beodeul grass, which has broader light and dark patches, tufts with highlights and a clear value structure, the candidate is a lower-contrast speckle on a mostly uniform base. Per-tile colour count is probably around 8-10, near the reference median, but the large base areas between clumps are a single flat colour, so it reads a bit thinner. The repeating accent dots look like stamped decoration. There are no outlines, which suits ground. Overall it is acceptable but slightly below the reference in richness and variety, and a careful artist would probably flag the tiling regularity and the thin shading ramp, so it fails on balance.
